summary: Fase 3 Listini retest. BUG FIX #1 (Richieste crash) VERIFIED FIXED: client Richieste tab renders biz order cards with itemized lines + '🔒 amount in escrow', pending order shows Cancel button; cancelling flips status to Cancelled (backend refund verified). BUG FIX #2 (Listino auto-select) VERIFIED FIXED: services[0] ('tecnico') is auto-selected on entry to /listino for biz-test-token-999. NOTE: seeded products are on 'lavanderia' (services[2]), so the seeded 'Lavaggio camicia' etc. only appear after tapping the Lavanderia chip; the auto-select itself works as per the useEffect fix. Full order flow (client→business Accept modal has NO price field →Segna consegnato→wallet) all working. CRUD: ADD (A2) and EDIT (A3) work correctly on /listino. DELETE (A4) FAILS on web: Alert.alert in listino/index.tsx does not fire its destructive callback on react-native-web, so the delete API is never called. Discovered a separate CRITICAL i18n structural bug: /app/frontend/src/i18n.ts has ONLY one dict opener (`it: {` at line 4) and never opens `en: {`; English strings (lines 1194-1262) are declared as duplicate keys inside the SAME `it:` block. Consequence: `strings.en` is undefined at runtime; the UI currently renders English text because duplicates overwrite the Italian values; and t('delete') (no such key anywhere) caused a red screen 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading delete)' in the destructive alert path. I applied a proper null-guard to LanguageContext.t (uses ?.[k] ?? … ?? k) so no more red screens, but the underlying i18n structure needs main agent restructuring.

ui_bugs.issue: Delete product does not work on web preview: Alert.alert(title, msg, [Cancel, Delete-destructive, onPress: api.deleteProduct]) never invokes the destructive callback under react-native-web. A4 flow blocked. Use the same web branch pattern used in (tabs)/richieste.tsx (confirmCancel): if (Platform.OS==='web') window.confirm(...) else Alert.alert(...). Reference: /app/frontend/app/listino/index.tsx:109-116

STRUCTURAL: only one language dict opener (`it: {` line 4) and no `en: {` block. All English strings (myListino, addProduct, ..., appTagline, heldInEscrow, ...) are declared as DUPLICATE keys inside the `it:` object (lines 1194-1262). At runtime `strings.en` is undefined, and because JS duplicate keys keep the LAST value, the Italian entries get overwritten by English so the app renders English strings even when lang='it'. The `t('delete')` red screen we hit on delete confirm was a direct consequence (no 'delete' key anywhere → fell through to strings.en[k] which is undefined). Reference: /app/frontend/src/i18n.ts:4, 1263-1266. Main agent must split into `it: {...}, en: {...}` and add missing 'delete' key.
Previous null-guard was incomplete: `return dict[k] || strings.en[k] || k;` still crashed when `strings.en` was undefined. FIXED IN THIS ITERATION using optional chaining + nullish coalescing.

rca_of_issue: Delete-product red-screen (surfaced during A4): the pressable calls Alert.alert with `t('delete')` in its buttons array. `strings.it` has no 'delete' key; the t() fallback was `strings.en[k]` — but `strings.en` is undefined because i18n.ts is missing the `en:` divider (all English strings sit inside `it:`). So `undefined.delete` → TypeError. Applied fix: made t() fully null-safe with optional chaining + nullish coalescing so any unresolved key returns `k` instead of crashing. However the delete callback still never fires on web because react-native-web's Alert.alert does not honour the destructive button in its default polyfill — separate fix needed via Platform.OS branch.
